title: Matthew Chapter 15 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Matthew chapter 15 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Matthew Chapter 15 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Matthew Chapter 15.

questions.question: Who came to Jesus asking about the disciples' actions?
questions.explanation: The scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem came to Jesus to question Him about His disciples' actions (Matthew 15:1).

questions.question: What tradition did the Pharisees claim the disciples transgressed?
questions.explanation: The Pharisees asked why the disciples did not wash their hands before eating, indicating they were transgressing the tradition of the elders (Matthew 15:2).

questions.question: What commandment did Jesus refer to when addressing the Pharisees?
questions.explanation: Jesus cited the commandment to honor one's father and mother when addressing the Pharisees' traditions (Matthew 15:4).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that what goes into the mouth defiles a man.
questions.explanation: Jesus clarified that it is not what goes into the mouth that defiles a man, but what comes out of the mouth (Matthew 15:11).

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the plants that His heavenly Father has not planted?
questions.explanation: Jesus stated that every plant not planted by His heavenly Father shall be rooted up (Matthew 15:13).

questions.question: True or False: The Pharisees were pleased with Jesus' teachings.
questions.explanation: The disciples informed Jesus that the Pharisees were offended by His sayings (Matthew 15:12).

questions.question: What did Jesus say about those who lead the blind?
options: They shall fall into the ditch
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall into the ditch
questions.explanation: Jesus warned that if the blind lead the blind, both shall fall into the ditch (Matthew 15:14).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus criticized the worship of the people as being in vain.
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasized that their worship was in vain because they taught for doctrines the commandments of men (Matthew 15:9).

questions.question: In which location did Jesus depart after addressing the Pharisees?
questions.explanation: After addressing the Pharisees, Jesus went to the coasts of Tyre and Sidon (Matthew 15:21).

questions.question: What did the woman of Canaan ask Jesus for?
questions.explanation: The woman of Canaan cried out to Jesus for mercy for her daughter, who was vexed with a devil (Matthew 15:22).

questions.question: True or False: Jesus immediately answered the woman's request for help.
questions.explanation: Jesus initially answered her not a word, indicating He did not respond immediately (Matthew 15:23).

medium.title: Matthew Chapter 15 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Matthew Chapter 15 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the tradition of the elders in relation to God's commandments?
options: Tradition is more important than commandments.
Tradition can nullify the commandments of God.
questions.correctAnswer: Tradition can nullify the commandments of God.
questions.explanation: Jesus criticized the Pharisees for making the commandment of God of none effect by their tradition, as stated in Matthew 15:6.

questions.question: According to Jesus, what defiles a man?
options: What comes out of the mouth.
questions.correctAnswer: What comes out of the mouth.
questions.explanation: Jesus taught that it is not what goes in at the mouth that defiles a man, but what comes out of the mouth, as stated in Matthew 15:11.

questions.question: What did Jesus say about the blind leading the blind?
options: Both shall fall into a ditch.
questions.correctAnswer: Both shall fall into a ditch.
questions.explanation: Jesus warned that if the blind lead the blind, both will fall into the ditch, as noted in Matthew 15:14.

questions.question: How did the disciples react when Jesus spoke about what defiles a man?
options: They were confused and asked for clarification.
questions.correctAnswer: They were confused and asked for clarification.
questions.explanation: The disciples approached Jesus and asked if He knew the Pharisees were offended by His saying, indicating their confusion, as recorded in Matthew 15:12.

questions.question: What does Matthew 15:19 say proceeds out of the heart?
questions.explanation: Matthew 15:19 lists evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false witness, and blasphemies as things that come from the heart and defile a man.

questions.question: What did the woman of Canaan request from Jesus?
questions.explanation: The woman of Canaan cried out to Jesus for mercy for her daughter, who was grievously vexed with a devil, as stated in Matthew 15:22.

questions.question: What was Jesus' initial response to the Canaanite woman?
questions.explanation: Initially, Jesus did not answer the woman of Canaan, which indicates His testing of her faith and persistence, as noted in Matthew 15:23.

questions.question: According to Matthew 15:26, what did Jesus say about taking children's bread?
options: It should be shared with the needy.
It is not right to give it to dogs.
It can be divided among all.
questions.correctAnswer: It is not right to give it to dogs.
questions.explanation: Jesus used this metaphor to express the priority of His ministry to the people of Israel, as stated in Matthew 15:26.

questions.question: What was the result of the woman's faith as expressed in her response to Jesus?
options: Jesus praised her for her humility.
questions.explanation: Jesus acknowledged the woman's great faith and granted her request, healing her daughter from that very hour, as stated in Matthew 15:28.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus said that to eat with unwashen hands defileth a man.
questions.explanation: Jesus clarified that eating with unwashen hands does not defile a man, but rather what comes out of the mouth does, as stated in Matthew 15:20.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus expressed compassion for the multitude that had followed Him for three days.
questions.explanation: Jesus showed compassion for the multitude because they had been with Him for three days and had nothing to eat, as noted in Matthew 15:32.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples were confident they could feed the multitude in the wilderness.
questions.explanation: The disciples questioned how they could feed such a great multitude in the wilderness, indicating their lack of confidence, as stated in Matthew 15:33.

hard.title: Matthew Chapter 15 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Matthew Chapter 15.

questions.question: What did Jesus mean when he said that what comes out of the mouth defiles a man?
options: Evil thoughts come from the heart
Traditions are more important than commandments
questions.correctAnswer: Evil thoughts come from the heart
questions.explanation: Jesus explains that it is the things that proceed out of the mouth that defile a man because they come from the heart, as stated in Matthew 15:18-19.

questions.question: How many loaves did Jesus have to feed the multitude?
questions.explanation: Jesus had seven loaves and a few little fishes to feed the multitude, as mentioned in Matthew 15:34.

questions.question: What was the response of Jesus to the Canaanite woman who asked for help?
questions.explanation: Jesus commended her great faith and granted her request, healing her daughter immediately, as stated in Matthew 15:28.

questions.question: What did the multitude do when they saw the miracles performed by Jesus?
options: They glorified the God of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: They glorified the God of Israel
questions.explanation: The multitude marveled at the miracles and glorified God for what they witnessed, as described in Matthew 15:31.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus stated that to eat with unwashen hands defiles a man.
questions.explanation: Jesus clarified that it is not what enters the mouth that defiles a man, but what comes out of it, as per Matthew 15:20.

questions.question: What did Jesus call the Pharisees in Matthew 15:7?
questions.explanation: Jesus referred to the Pharisees as hypocrites, fulfilling the prophecy of Isaiah, as stated in Matthew 15:7.

questions.question: What was the Canaanite woman's response when Jesus referred to taking children's bread and casting it to dogs?
questions.explanation: The woman humbly accepted Jesus' words, indicating that even dogs eat the crumbs from their masters' table, as seen in Matthew 15:27.

questions.question: Which Old Testament theme resonates with Jesus' teaching about honoring one’s parents?
questions.explanation: Jesus cites the commandment 'Honor thy father and mother' from the Old Testament, indicating its importance over human traditions in Matthew 15:4.

questions.question: What does the term 'great faith' signify in the context of Matthew 15:28?
questions.explanation: Jesus commended the Canaanite woman for her great faith, recognizing her belief in His ability to heal her daughter, as stated in Matthew 15:28.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus was initially sent to the Gentiles.
questions.explanation: Jesus specifically stated that He was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, as mentioned in Matthew 15:24.

questions.question: What significant action did Jesus perform with the seven loaves and fishes?
options: He broke them and gave thanks
He divided them among the disciples
questions.correctAnswer: He broke them and gave thanks
questions.explanation: Jesus took the loaves and fishes, gave thanks, and then broke them to distribute to the multitude, as stated in Matthew 15:36.

questions.question: Which literary device is illustrated by the Canaanite woman's response to Jesus?
questions.explanation: The woman's response demonstrates a paradox by acknowledging her lowly status while still asserting faith in Jesus' mercy, which resonates with the theme of humility.

questions.question: How many baskets of broken meat were collected after the feeding of the four thousand?
questions.explanation: After feeding the multitude, seven baskets of broken meat were collected, as described in Matthew 15:37.

theological.title: Matthew Chapter 15 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Matthew Chapter 15 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is illustrated by Jesus' response to the Pharisees regarding tradition and God's commandments?
questions.explanation: Jesus emphasizes that human traditions can sometimes contradict God's commandments, thus affirming the authority of scripture over tradition (Matthew 15:3).

questions.question: Which attribute of God is revealed through the commandment to honor one's parents?
questions.explanation: The commandment to honor one's father and mother highlights God's authority in establishing family relationships and moral order (Matthew 15:4).

questions.question: In Matthew 15, what does Jesus indicate is the true source of defilement?
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that it is what comes out of the mouth, stemming from the heart, that defiles a person, rather than external rituals (Matthew 15:18-20).

questions.question: What does the interaction with the Canaanite woman teach about Jesus' mission?
options: He came solely for the Jews
He was indifferent to the plight of others
questions.correctAnswer: He came solely for the Jews
questions.explanation: Jesus indicates that his mission is primarily to the lost sheep of Israel, highlighting the Jewish context of his ministry (Matthew 15:24).

questions.question: What does Jesus mean when he says, 'Let them alone: they be blind leaders of the blind'?
questions.explanation: Jesus points out the spiritual blindness of the Pharisees, indicating that they lead others astray due to their lack of true understanding (Matthew 15:14).

questions.question: What doctrine of sin is illustrated by Jesus' teaching on what defiles a person?
questions.explanation: Jesus clarifies that personal sin stems from the heart, indicating that moral failure originates within rather than from external sources (Matthew 15:18-19).

questions.question: How does the healing of the multitude relate to the theme of compassion in Matthew 15?
options: It shows Jesus' rejection of the unworthy
It highlights Jesus' concern for physical and spiritual needs
questions.correctAnswer: It highlights Jesus' concern for physical and spiritual needs
questions.explanation: Jesus expresses compassion for the multitude, indicating his care for their physical hunger as well as their spiritual condition (Matthew 15:32).

questions.question: What does the phrase 'great is thy faith' signify in the context of the Canaanite woman's request?
options: The importance of faith in Jesus' healing
questions.correctAnswer: The importance of faith in Jesus' healing
questions.explanation: Jesus commends the woman for her faith, indicating that faith plays a crucial role in receiving healing and mercy from him (Matthew 15:28).

questions.question: What does the feeding of the four thousand demonstrate about Jesus' authority?
questions.explanation: The miraculous feeding shows Jesus' authority over nature and his power to provide abundantly for those in need (Matthew 15:36-37).

questions.question: What role does the heart play in Jesus' teaching about defilement?
options: It is the source of good actions
It is irrelevant in spiritual matters
It is the source of evil thoughts and actions
questions.correctAnswer: It is the source of evil thoughts and actions
questions.explanation: Jesus teaches that the heart is where evil thoughts originate, which in turn lead to sinful actions, thereby defiling a person (Matthew 15:18-19).

questions.question: How does the response of Jesus to the Canaanite woman reflect His view on faith?
options: He only accepts faith from Jews
He tests faith to reveal its depth
He values faith only in public settings
questions.correctAnswer: He tests faith to reveal its depth
questions.explanation: Jesus initially appears indifferent to the woman's plea, which serves to reveal the depth and persistence of her faith, leading to her daughter's healing (Matthew 15:26-28).

questions.question: What does Jesus' command to sit down indicate about his approach to ministry?
options: He is indifferent to crowd behavior
He prioritizes spiritual over physical needs
questions.explanation: By commanding the multitude to sit down, Jesus establishes order and prepares for a miraculous provision, indicating his thoughtful approach to ministry (Matthew 15:35).

questions.question: What can be inferred about the significance of the seven baskets of leftovers after feeding the multitude?
questions.explanation: The seven baskets of leftovers demonstrate not only the miracle of feeding the multitude but also God's abundant provision beyond immediate needs (Matthew 15:37).

questions.question: What principle regarding worship does Jesus teach in Matthew 15?
options: Worship must come from the heart
Worship is exclusively for the Jewish people
questions.correctAnswer: Worship must come from the heart
questions.explanation: Jesus critiques the worship of those whose hearts are far from God, emphasizing that true worship requires sincerity and alignment with God's will (Matthew 15:8-9).

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Jesus was indifferent to the plight of the Gentiles. What does Matthew 15:21-28 actually teach?
options: He valued faith from all people
He was harsh to all outsiders
questions.correctAnswer: He valued faith from all people
questions.explanation: While initially addressing the lost sheep of Israel, Jesus ultimately responds to the woman's faith, demonstrating that his grace extends beyond ethnic boundaries (Matthew 15:28).
